title: Database Cascade Failure – Slow Query Avalanche
description: Multiple services are degraded. Trace the dependency chain, identify the true root cause (not the red herring), and apply the correct remediation.

initial_alerts.message: frontend: HTTP 503 error rate at 34% – users cannot complete checkout
order-service: p99 latency 28,000ms (threshold: 2000ms). Request queue backing up.
order-service: CPU at 89% – possible compute saturation
inventory-service: p99 latency 15,000ms – database calls timing out

frontend.message: Retry budget exhausted for order-service – returning 503 to user

order-service.message: DB query timeout after 25000ms: SELECT * FROM orders JOIN order_items ON ... WHERE customer_id=? [full table scan detected]
DB query timeout after 25000ms: SELECT * FROM orders JOIN order_items ON ...
Thread pool saturation: 200/200 threads blocked on DB calls. New requests queuing.
Deployment v2.4.1 → v2.4.2 completed 18 minutes ago

inventory-service.message: postgres query timeout: SELECT stock_level FROM inventory WHERE sku IN (?,?,?,...) [1000 items]
Connection pool exhausted: all 50 connections waiting on postgres-primary

postgres-primary.message: pg_stat_activity: 847 active connections (max_connections=1000). Lock contention detected.
Slow query detected (24.8s): SELECT o.*, oi.* FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.id=oi.order_id WHERE o.customer_id=$1 — Seq Scan on orders (cost=0.00..892847.00 rows=2847293)
Slow query detected (23.1s): SELECT o.*, oi.* FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.id=oi.order_id WHERE o.customer_id=$1 — Seq Scan on orders
Index orders_customer_id_idx: INVALID (migration in progress or failed). Falling back to Seq Scan.
Running migration 20240210_add_customer_index: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_customer_id_idx ON orders(customer_id)

diagnostic_results.explain_query postgres-primary: EXPLAIN output: Seq Scan on orders (cost=0.00..892847.00 rows=2847293 width=284). Index orders_customer_id_idx exists but is INVALID – created CONCURRENTLY and failed at 67% due to a conflicting lock. All queries falling back to sequential scan of 2.8M row table.
diagnostic_results.check_migrations postgres-primary: Migration status: 20240210_add_customer_index – FAILED (lock timeout at step 3/4). Index left in INVALID state. Fix: DROP INDEX orders_customer_id_idx; then re-run migration during low-traffic window, OR: REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_customer_id_idx
diagnostic_results.heap_dump order-service: 200 threads blocked in com.orders.db.OrderRepository.findByCustomerId() waiting for DB response. CPU spike is from thread contention + GC pressure, not a compute issue.
diagnostic_results.ping order-service: order-service pod is running but all threads blocked on DB calls

restart_order_service.note: order-service restarted. New pods immediately hit same slow queries. No improvement. Root cause is in postgres-primary.

reindex_invalid_index.description: REINDEX CONCURRENTLY the invalid customer index on orders table
reindex_invalid_index.note: REINDEX CONCURRENTLY completed in 4m12s. Index orders_customer_id_idx is now VALID. Query times: 24,800ms → 8ms. All downstream services recovering. p99 latency normalizing.

drop_invalid_index.description: DROP the invalid index to stop seq scans (temporary fix, loses index benefit)
drop_invalid_index.note: Invalid index dropped. Queries now complete in ~180ms (no index benefit but no INVALID index overhead). Services recovering. Recommend scheduling reindex during maintenance window.

scale_order_service.note: Scaled to 10 replicas. All new pods also blocked on DB. DB connection count now 3000/1000 – connection pool exhausted. Things are worse.

increase_db_connections.note: max_connections increased. More connections established but all stuck on slow queries. Root cause unchanged.

grader_criteria.red_herring: order-service CPU spike is caused by thread contention waiting on DB, not a compute issue
